problem: Cell index 7 is marked 'live' but nothing in the caption or pointers explains it, and index 7 is data bit D6 = 1, not any special bit. A student may think bit 7 or the MSB is being highlighted, when the point the text makes is that the first data bit after start (index 1) is 1. The cell value itself is right.
fix: Move the 'live' mark to cell 1 (D0, the first data bit, which is 1) and label it 'first data bit = 1', or delete the unexplained mark and keep only the start and stop pointers.

problem: 'Hardware sets TI = 1 after the stop bit leaves TXD' is one bit time too late. In mode 1 the 8051 sets TI when the 8th data bit finishes and the stop bit begins, which is why back-to-back bytes can be sent by loading SBUF right after clearing TI.
fix: Write: 'hardware sets TI = 1 at the end of the 8th data bit, when transmission of the stop bit begins, so SBUF is free for the next byte.'

problem: EIA-232 is the formal name of the standard itself, not a nickname used by some syllabi, so grouping it with 'serial port' and 'COM port' as alternative course names is misleading.
fix: Write: 'RS-232 is also known by its formal standard name EIA-232; in everyday use it is called the serial port or COM port.'
